materiality: The fp8_ds_mla cache writer previously stored arbitrary FP32 per-tile scales even though SM90 and SM100 FlashMLA readers quantize those scale fields through different reduced representations; the writer and reader can therefore disagree about the effective quantization scale for the same cached bytes.

The successor changes all three known writers—native CUDA, fused DeepSeek-V3.2 Triton, and Kimi-K3 shared prefill/decode—to a power-of-two scale contract, making this a cross-backend KV-cache correctness boundary rather than a throughput-only kernel change.
disconfirmingEvidence: Upstream reported one candidate serving run slower than its control and explicitly made no performance claim.
The PR description states that a full SM90 model evaluation was still outstanding; source/kernel tests and GB300/SM103 evidence must not be treated as SM90 model qualification.

materiality: A ragged mixed/warmup decode batch can report requires_padding=false and then enter a uniform reshape even when num_decode_tokens is not divisible by the number of decode sequences, producing a serving crash; the observed upstream failure was eight decode tokens over six requests on SM120/GB10 TP2.
The successor couples pack and unpack selection to a shared padded-path predicate, making batch-shape interpretation a runtime correctness and availability boundary for sparse-indexer serving.
disconfirmingEvidence: The upstream source comment explicitly says token-count divisibility is necessary but not sufficient to prove a uniform batch; a divisible ragged shape such as decode_lens=[1,2,3] still depends on requires_padding being correct.
Upstream end-to-end evidence is specific to 2x DGX Spark/GB10 TP2 and does not qualify other architectures, topologies, speculative modes or every ragged shape.
